title: Global average pooling hurts convergence speed
description: The authors found that using global average pooling increased model stability but hurt convergence speed, so they had to find a middle ground.
canonical_description: global average pooling increases stability but reduces convergence speed

evidence.anchor: global average pooling increased model stability but hurt convergence speed
evidence.quote: We found global average pooling increased model stability but hurt convergence speed.

verdict.reasoning: No candidate papers were deep-read, so there is no evidence the gap has been addressed.

ranking.feasibility_reasoning: Focused, well-scoped problem: the effect of a single architectural component (GAP) on a single measurable property (convergence speed). Data is plentiful (ImageNet, CIFAR, etc.) and compute needs are moderate — a few GPUs suffice for systematic controlled experiments. Methodologically mature: many alternatives to GAP already exist (adaptive pooling, strided convs, attention pooling, hybrid approaches), and convergence speed is straightforward to measure via loss curves or epochs-to-target. The main difficulty is disentangling the stability–speed trade-off, which may be inherent rather than fixable, but even characterizing the boundary more precisely would constitute real progress. Score slightly below 0.75 because the gap may reflect a fundamental trade-off that no simple modification fully resolves.
